This page (Page 6) details the career support and employability opportunities available to students at Nottingham Trent University (NTU). It highlights specialist employability support, including one-to-one advice, access to careers fairs, and global employer networks. The university offers a Global Employability Award for recognizing student experiences and skills. A key feature is the availability of work placements, with NTU being ranked in the top 5 UK universities for undergraduate students on one-year placements (HESA 2021/22). The page also mentions shorter placements and projects that allow students to work directly with employers. Students are encouraged to develop professional skills such as planning, communication, analysis, creativity, cooperation, and problem-solving.

- NTU experience provides opportunities and support for success in the UK and globally.
- Specialist employability support includes one-to-one advice, careers fairs, and global employer networks.
- Students can earn the Global Employability Award for their experiences and skills.
- NTU is in the top 5 UK universities for the number of undergraduate students on one-year placements (HESA 2021/22).
- Many courses offer a one-year placement, while others offer shorter placements and employer projects.
- Students develop professional skills like planning, communication, analysis, creativity, cooperation, and problem-solving.
- Advice on working in the UK after graduation is available.

pages.summary:
This page provides advice for parents and family members of international students considering studying at Nottingham Trent University (NTU). It highlights two key support services: Country Advisors in the International Office who offer guidance on studying at NTU, and NTU Education Counsellors, external agencies that assist with the application process and visa applications. The page also details the dedicated International Student Support team, which offers face-to-face, email, and one-to-one appointment support for issues including student visas, graduate routes, visa extensions, and settling into life in Nottingham. A photograph shows a graduate named Aneurin Lau from Hong Kong celebrating his graduation with his family.

**Text Evidence:**
- The university offers advice and information to support families of international students.
- Specialist Country Advisors in the International Office can advise on any aspect of studying at NTU.
- NTU Education Counsellors are external agencies that can help with the application process and visa applications in the family's country.
- The International Student Support team provides excellent services, including visa application advice (Student visa, Graduate route, and visa extension) and support with settling into student life.
- The support team is available on all campuses via face-to-face contact, email, or one-to-one appointments.

The text highlights how the foundation year helped them adapt to university life in the UK, emphasizing the supportive community and smooth transition provided by NTIC. The page also includes contact information for NTIC, which is part of Kaplan International, along with social media icons and a website URL.

**Text Evidence:**
- Terry Tan, from China, studied the NTIC Foundation course and progressed to BSc Sports Science and Management.
- Jannah Aboelghar, from an unspecified location, studied the NTIC Foundation course and progressed to BSc (Hons) Ecology and Conservation.
- Both students state that the NTIC Foundation course prepared them well for university and made their transition to NTU much easier.
- Terry Tan mentions the course gave him time to adapt to teaching habits, learning atmosphere, and living environment in the UK.
- Jannah Aboelghar describes her experience as "the most fun year" she has ever had and praises the diverse, inclusive, and supportive community at NTIC.

**Visual Evidence:**
<image_summary>Two Polaroid-style photos are displayed on the left side of the page. The top photo shows a young man named Terry wearing a face mask. The bottom photo shows a young woman named Jannah smiling.</image_summary>

elements.text: Before I progressed to NTU, I studied the foundation course at NTIC. I think it prepared me well for my university course. It gave me time to adapt to the teaching habits, learning atmosphere and living environment in the UK in advance. In my first year at the University, I think I adapted to NTU and life in the UK much better than other international students who had not done a preparation course.
NTIC Foundation course, progressing to BSc Sports Science and Management

Looking back, I can say my experience on the Foundation year at NTIC was the most fun year I have ever had! The sense of community was great, and it was very diverse and inclusive. It was very easy for me to feel part of the community, and I keep in touch with my NTIC friends.

Being part of NTIC made my transition to university much easier. They made my transition to university smooth; they provided great support and the team was very approachable and helpful during my transition to NTU."
NTIC Foundation course, progressing to BSc (Hons) Ecology and Conservation
Nottingham Trent International College (part of Kaplan International)

sections.title: More about NTU
sections.summary:
<section_card>
SECTION: More about NTU (Pages 36-56)

TOPICS: University campuses, academic schools, student facilities, language programme, teaching quality, investment in resources, student support services, global opportunities, professional accreditations, accommodation

TEXT_EVIDENCE:
- There are eight Academic Schools located over the City, Clifton, and Brackenhurst campuses, plus Confetti campuses in Nottingham and London (Page 36)
- The City Campus is a cosmopolitan, bustling campus right in the city centre, only five minutes' walk to shops and the excitement of a busy student city (Page 36)
- The City Campus hosts the Nottingham Business School, Nottingham School of Art & Design, School of Architecture, Design and the Built Environment, Nottingham Law School, School of Social Sciences, Journalism and Media Hub, Confetti Institute of Creative Technologies, Nottingham Institute for Languages and Intercultural Communication (NILIC), and Nottingham Trent International College (NTIC) (Page 36)
- Clifton Campus is a "friendly, vibrant student village" located six kilometres from the centre of Nottingham, with a bus service every 10 minutes to the City Campus (Page 37)
- Clifton Campus hosts the School of Arts and Humanities, School of Science and Technology, and the Nottingham Institute of Health and Allied Professions (Page 37)
- Brackenhurst Campus is described as a "beautiful campus in the countryside," about a 45-minute drive from Nottingham (Page 37)
- Students from the School of Animal, Rural and Environmental Sciences will be studying at Brackenhurst Campus (Page 37)
- Confetti Nottingham is located in Nottingham's flourishing Creative Quarter, just a short walk from NTU City Campus (Page 38)
- Confetti London is opening in September 2023 and is situated in Whitechapel, East London (Page 38)
- The photo on Page 39 shows students walking outside the main entrance on Goldsmiths Street at the NTU City Campus (Page 39)
- Students at NTU can learn a language for free while studying, requiring only a small refundable deposit and offering flexible study hours of 2 hours per week or more (Page 40)
- Languages offered include French, Spanish, Chinese, Japanese, Arabic, German, or Italian (Page 40)
- Lecturers have extensive experience in industry, research, and the professions, ensuring high-quality education in the UK (Page 41)
- Students benefit from inspirational guest lecturers and practical experience, which helps them develop confidence (Page 41)
- International students are valued for their contributions, challenges, fresh ideas, and new perspectives (Page 41)
- NTU has invested over £450 million in facilities and campuses in the last 15 years (Page 42)
- The award-winning libraries provide access to over 650,000 electronic books and journals and approximately 300,000 printed books, open 24/7 during term time (Page 42)
- IT facilities include loan laptops, group and individual study spaces, thousands of computers, 24-hour access, and specialist course-related software (Page 42)
- Global Lounges are available on the City and Clifton campuses, offering language practice, a communal area, cultural events, and a resource centre (Page 43)
- All campuses have green spaces for fresh air and a peaceful atmosphere (Page 43)
- The Chaplaincy team provides pastoral support, prayer, meditation, and reflection, including Jewish, Muslim, Catholic, and Methodist chaplains (Page 43)
- The Chaplaincy team includes Muslim prayer rooms across all campuses (Page 43)
- Amazing sport facilities include a 100-station gym, fitness studios, outdoor sports pitches, an indoor tennis centre, a sports therapy suite, sports halls, a dance studio, and a 10m climbing wall (Page 44)
- A dedicated music practice space is available for all abilities and musical interests (Page 44)
- An incredible range of venues, societies, sports clubs, events, and initiatives are available across all campuses (Page 44)
- The Global Summer School offers courses for everyone to learn something new, meet friends from around the world, and experience Nottingham (Page 45)
- Participants in the Global Summer School can earn UK credits upon course completion (Page 45)
- Kunwar Thapar, a 2022 participant in the Design and Innovation in Business program, praised the experience of working with people from other nations (Page 45)
- The Nottingham School of Art & Design has been teaching art and design since 1843 and is among the top 10% of art and design providers in the QS World University Rankings (Page 48)
- A new Design and Digital Arts building will launch in 2024 on the City Campus (Page 48)
- The School of Architecture, Design and the Built Environment offers industry-focused courses accredited by RIBA, The Institution of Structural Engineers, CSD, The PWI, The Institution for Rail, The Chartered Institute of Building (CIOB), RICS, and the Engineering Council (Page 49)
- The School of Animal, Rural and Environmental Sciences is one of the leading centres in the UK for animal and environmental sciences and was ranked Top 20 in the UK for Food Science in the Times Good University Guide 2023 (Page 50)
- The Equestrian Centre has extensive and unique facilities, including indoor and outdoor riding and research arenas (Page 50)
- The School of Arts and Humanities is ranked "Top 10 in the UK for Creative Writing" in the Times Good University Guide 2023 (Page 51)
- Journalism courses at the School of Arts and Humanities are highly regarded within the profession due to industry-standard facilities (Page 51)
- Nottingham Business School (NBS) is an AACSB and EQUIS-accredited business school with additional accreditations from CIM, EFMD, CIPD, MRS Evidence Matters, and CIPFA (Page 52)
- Nottingham Law School has an outstanding reputation for excellent legal education built on strong industry relationships, research strength, and facilities (Page 53)
- Many staff at Nottingham Law School are experienced lawyers, some still in practice (Page 53)
- The award-winning Legal Advice Centre allows students to work with qualified solicitors on real-life cases with members of the public (Page 53)
- The School of Science and Technology is located at the Clifton Campus and is described as one of the UK's most pioneering science and technology schools (Page 54)
- The School of Science and Technology holds professional accreditations from the RSC, IET, and IOP (Page 54)
- It claims to have one of the best teaching and research laboratories in the UK (Page 54)
- The School of Social Sciences and Nottingham Institute of Education emphasize diversity, high standards, globally acclaimed research, and well-trained graduates in key frontline services (Page 55)
- Courses are designed with professionals and public organizations (Page 55)
- There is a large psychology department with over 150 academics (Page 55)
- Some courses are accredited by the British Psychological Society (BPS) (Page 55)
- Finding a happy living environment is important to the student experience (Page 56)
- NTU offers a huge range of both University and private accommodation to suit every budget (Page 56)
- All accommodation is high quality, modern, and meets high safety standards (Page 56)
- Accommodation is located in convenient locations on or close to campus (Page 56)
- Flexible accommodation contracts are available for Pre-sessional English (PEAP) students and those starting a Masters in January (Page 56)
- Key benefits include safety and security, a choice of en suite or shared facilities, great locations, free Wi-Fi, and included utility bills (Page 56)

pages.ocr_text: Your home away from home Being happy where you're living is such an important part of your student experience. That's why we have a fantastic choice of accommodation available for you, and it's really important to start your research early. We offer a huge range of both University and private accommodation to suit every budget. All our accommodation is high quality, modern, and meets high safety standards. And it is located in convenient locations on - or close to - campus. We can offer flexible accommodation contracts, perfect if you're a Pre-sessional English (PEAP) student or if you're starting a Masters in January. Staying in NTU accommodation, you can count on: Safety and security A choice of en suite or shared facilities Great locations on or close to campus Free Wi-Fi, and your utility bills included in your rent Easy access to all our support services

pages.ocr_text: International Scholarships We award many scholarships to international students who have offers to study at NTU. These are highly prestigious, competitive awards, worth up to half of your tuition fee. Our scholars have gone on to become strong and highly valued ambassadors for the University. All scholarships available are listed on our website, with application advice and deadlines. If you're progressing from one of our partner universities, you may be eligible for a partner progression discount. You can still apply for a scholarship, but you won't be awarded both – the higher amount would be deducted from your tuition fees. "How did I feel when I won an NTU scholarship?" I was overwhelmed with joy and excitement. This has opened new opportunities to finally achieve my dreams of becoming an engineer. And it has reduced some of the financial constraints significantly for my family and I." Tremaine Maskall, Belize "My parents were very excited and surprised when they knew I got the scholarship. They said I was so lucky, and they appreciated NTU for providing me with the scholarship." Wen Shou-Yu, Taiwan

pages.ocr_text: Budgeting There are many ways to save money while you're here - using your student card for discounts in shops and on transport, for example. Some of our international students choose to work part-time to get some extra income while gaining valuable experience. Your daily, weekly and monthly costs will mostly be for your accommodation, food, entertainment and bills. It's important to be prepared and to budget carefully - you'll find more advice on our website. Approximate costs of studying in Nottingham per month: Based on National Student Money Survey 2022 You will need to bring enough money to cover your living costs at least equivalent to the £1,023 per month required for visa application purposes (£1,334 for London Confetti campus).
